items.title: Spaniards shut down country over high housing prices

items.title: This Ontario legion got over 500 new members this year
items.summary_auto: Legions across Waterloo region are seeing a massive boost in new members this year. The Royal Canadian Legion has been encouraging new members to join with no fees this year to celebrate its centennial. CBC's Aastha Shetty visited Branch 272 in Hespeler to hear more about what's drawing new members in.

items.title: Polish woman shares harrowing WW II story with Sask. community
items.summary_auto: Decades after rebuilding their lives in Saskatchewan, Polish survivors are working to ensure those experiences are never forgotten.

items.title: N.B. veteran to wear replica medals on Remembrance Day after originals were stolen
items.summary_auto: A 91-year-old New Brunswick veteran thought he might have to spend this Remembrance Day without his medals after his were stolen from his home this summer. But that won't be the case for retired lieutenant-colonel Alan Kennedy. While they aren't the originals, the replicas, made possible because of the effort of a fellow veteran and kindness of a local businesswoman, will be pinned over his heart on Nov. 11.

items.title: Stellantis auto plant sale draws optimism, hurt in Brampton, Ont., after 2,000 jobs lost

items.title: Congo's Ebola outbreak tops 11,000 cases as disease keeps spreading

items.title: 3 dead, driver arrested after vehicle plows into pedestrians in Los Angeles
items.summary_auto: The 61-year-old driver of a minivan that killed three people when it  crashed outside a Los Angeles metro station during rush hour was arrested on three counts of murder, a police spokesperson said Wednesday.

items.title: Canadian family finds long-lost WW II baby in England after 80 years
items.summary_auto: Rod Anderson grew up in the United Kingdom always wondering who his father was. At 81 years old, he received a call out of the blue this year that stunned him. It turns out his father was a Canadian soldier stationed in Britain during the Second World War. A family in New Brunswick spent almost 20 years trying to find him.

items.title: Canadians fought a war in Afghanistan. Why do we struggle to talk about it?
items.summary_auto: Is Afghanistan in danger of becoming Canada's forgotten war? Parliament is struggling with a bill that would designate the 13-year conflict — where more than 40,000 Canadians served — as a war. The prime minister's Veterans' Week statement mentions the tragedy in Wainwright and service in the first Gulf War, but not Afghanistan. And an increasing number of veterans say the war and understanding what happened is now slipping from the national conscience.

items.title: For this Afghanistan vet, no memorial can ever rival this hallowed ground
items.summary_auto: On Remembrance Day, retired colonel Mark Gasparotto attends the service at Canada's National Military Cemetery in Ottawa. Afterward, the Afghanistan veteran walks among the rows of graves where he recognizes many of the names engraved on the headstones.

items.title: Are we alone? Institute searching for alien signals is using a new way to answer that age-old question
items.summary_auto: Where are all the aliens? We've yet to find life outside of that on Earth, but that doesn't mean scientists aren't looking. In fact, the search for extraterrestrial intelligence is going strong, and now the SETI Institute is listening for radio signals in a new way.

items.title: Carney embarks on a worldwide summit tour to build bridges with Europe and Asia
items.summary_auto: Prime Minister Mark Carney will travel around the world over the next week as he attends the summits of the European Political Community, the Association of Southeast Asian Nations, the Francophonie and Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation. Both defence and trade will be discussed in a range of multilateral and bilateral meetings.

items.title: This veteran thinks his brain cancer is linked to his deployment. He pushed for special benefits — and won
items.summary_auto: It took three attempts for a retired military officer diagnosed with a rare brain cancer to receive special benefits from Veterans Affairs Canada. Bruce Mayo researched and found others with the same diagnosis who also served in Southwest Asia. Mayo wants Canada to change its presumptive injury list, putting it in line with U.S. policy.

items.title: A Christmas care package for a Canadian WWII soldier was left behind. 80 years later, his family is getting it
items.summary_auto: Descendants of a Second World War soldier from Manitoba are thrilled by the discovery of a Christmas care package hidden for more than 80 years in the attic of an English mansion. The package will soon be returned to the soldier's son, who hopes to put it on display.

items.title: Stacy Keach, stage actor and Mike Hammer star, dead at 85
